content: Chlorothiazide, commonly referred to as a water pill, is prescribed to manage high blood pressure and fluid retention caused by various conditions, including heart disease. It works by prompting the kidneys to eliminate excess water and salt from the body through urine. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Chlorothiazide is available in tablet and liquid forms for oral administration. It is typically taken once or twice daily. If prescribed once daily, it should be taken in the morning. If prescribed twice daily, doses should be taken in the morning and late afternoon to minimize nighttime urination. It is recommended to take this medication with meals or a snack. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take chlorothiazide exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. While chlorothiazide helps control high blood pressure, it does not cure it. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Chlorothiazide may also be used to treat diabetes insipidus, certain electrolyte imbalances, and to prevent kidney stones in patients with elevated calcium levels in their blood. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your specific condition with your doctor. Before taking chlorothiazide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to chlorothiazide, sulfa drugs, or any other medications. Provide a list of all medications, supplements, and vitamins you are taking, especially corticosteroids, lithium, diabetes medications, probenecid, and cholestyramine or colestipol (which should be taken at least one hour after chlorothiazide). Notify your doctor if you have a history of diabetes, gout, or kidney, liver, thyroid, or parathyroid disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking chlorothiazide, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, if you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking chlorothiazide. Avoid unnecessary or prolonged sun exposure, and use protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as this medication may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight. Follow your doctor’s dietary instructions while taking chlorothiazide. Your doctor may recommend increasing potassium-rich foods, such as bananas, prunes, raisins, and orange juice, in your diet. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Frequent urination is a common side effect that typically subsides after a few weeks of use. If you experience dizziness or lightheadedness when standing up, rise slowly from a sitting or lying position. Notify your doctor if you experience severe or persistent symptoms, such as muscle weakness, dizziness, cramps, thirst, stomach pain, upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, headache, or hair loss. If you experience severe side effects, such as a sore throat with fever, unusual bleeding or bruising, severe skin rash with peeling, or difficulty breathing or swallowing, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store chlorothiazide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Prevent the oral liquid form from freezing. Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory for regular blood pressure monitoring and occasional blood tests. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
